title: Jumble of Jellyfish
description: This photo of upside-down jellyfish was taken for the October 2018 issue of National Geographic. As their name suggests, these jellies rest upside down with their bells on the sea floor and their oral arms reaching upward, allowing them to absorb light and produce food through photosynthesis. They range in size (the largest in this photo is 1.7 inches across) and shades of brown, green, and blue, making it easy for them to blend into the shallow waters they frequent in both tropical and subtropical climates.
translated_description: 这张倒立水母的照片拍摄于《国家地理》2018年10月刊。正如其名，这些水母将伞面朝下栖息于海底，口腕向上伸展，以此吸收光线并通过光合作用制造养分。它们的体型各异（本图中最大的一只直径约1.7英寸），体色呈现棕、绿、蓝等深浅不一的色调，使其能轻易融入常出没的热带及亚热带浅水海域。
